SOLID BENIGN LESIONS — THE BIG THREE
F > M; incidental; the commonest benign liver
No treatment and no follow-up; the OCP need not
Women on OCP; anabolic steroids; obesity /
MRI subtyping; fat / haemorrhage; NO central
Yes — bleeds & can become HCC (↑ β-catenin,
Stop OCP + weight loss; male or β-catenin →
resect any size; female ≥5 cm → resect after
Marked steatosis; diffuse fat on MRI
Atypia; retains no fat; overlaps HCC
(paromomycin / diloxanide furoate); aspirate only if no

Eggshell calcification; water-lily sign; daughter cysts;
Ovarian-type stroma; NO communication with the biliary

Very common incidental finding; thin-walled, no septa or
No follow-up whatever the size; laparoscopic deroofing
mgmt; volume-reduction or transplant if severe
FNH has a central scar and no malignant potential — do not resect. The adenoma is the lesion that bleeds and can transform to HCC.
Hepatocellular adenoma in a man, or a β-catenin subtype, is resected at any size; in women, stop the OCP, advise weight loss and reassess a
Never percutaneously biopsy or blindly aspirate a suspected hydatid cyst — spillage risks anaphylaxis and peritoneal dissemination.
A mucinous cystic neoplasm is premalignant: it needs complete resection, not deroofing. Ovarian-type stroma and absent biliary
communication distinguish it from IPMN of the bile duct.
Amoebic liver abscess is treated medically (metronidazole + a luminal agent); drainage is reserved for non-response, large / left-lobe cysts or
A simple hepatic cyst needs no follow-up regardless of size; deroof only when symptomatic. Avoid biopsy of a haemangioma — giant lesions
Sources: EASL Clinical Practice Guidelines on the management of benign liver tumours (J Hepatol 2016; 65:386–398) · EASL Clinical Practice Guidelines on the management of cystic liver
diseases (J Hepatol 2022) · WHO-IWGE ultrasound classification of cystic echinococcosis (CE1–CE5). HCA molecular subtypes: Zucman-Rossi / Bordeaux classification.
Malignant-potential axis and PAIR size thresholds are a teaching simplification — stage and treat on the full imaging and MDT assessment.
